Always conjugated in the past tense, for example 'Added login form'
Conjugated in the future tense, indicating what will be done in the following commit

c2a085fc6935.domanda: What should you never do with a file that still contains the '<<<<<<<' markers?
c2a085fc6935.spiegazione: You should never commit a file that still contains conflict markers: the code would be broken.
risposte: Save it to disk after opening it in a text editor
Open it in a code editor to read it better
Read it carefully to understand which parts are in conflict

1d10390ae051.domanda: Why should you not manually modify the .git folder?
1d10390ae051.spiegazione: The .git folder is entirely managed by Git via its commands: it should never be modified manually.
risposte: Because the folder is always recreated from scratch on every commit
Because it is protected by the operating system and cannot be opened
Because it is located on the remote server and not on the local machine

26f3593c7514.domanda: What mood should be used for a commit subject line?
26f3593c7514.spiegazione: The imperative mood is used: 'Add login validation'. Test: 'If applied, this commit will ___' must complete correctly.
risposte: Always expressed as a direct question
Always conjugated in the past tense
In the present imperative, like a command (Add, not Added)

8234153fc2e6.domanda: In the analogy with Google Docs, what does a Git commit correspond to?
8234153fc2e6.spiegazione: Each saved version in Google Docs corresponds to a commit; the list of versions is the commit history.

85be5af5a3d2.domanda: Which phrase completes the test for a good subject line?
85be5af5a3d2.spiegazione: Useful test: the subject line should complete 'If applied, this commit will ___', which encourages the use of the imperative mood.

2a9f8c6822a6.domanda: Which command lists remote tracking branches (e.g., origin/main)?
2a9f8c6822a6.spiegazione: git branch -a lists all branches, including remote tracking branches such as origin/main.

1d029800b845.domanda: Which command lists local branches, with an asterisk on the current one?
1d029800b845.spiegazione: git branch alone lists local branches and marks the current one with an asterisk (*).

a5fd71e40acf.domanda: Which git reset option permanently discards changes?
a5fd71e40acf.spiegazione: A describes keeping staged changes, B discards them permanently, C moves them to the working directory (default), D keeps them unstaged.

4b0e5bbe907e.domanda: What structure do commits form in Git?
4b0e5bbe907e.spiegazione: Commits form a DAG (directed acyclic graph): each commit points to its parent, and 'acyclic' means that a commit can never be an ancestor of itself.
risposte: A directed acyclic graph (DAG) where each commit points to its parent commit

9c7145142ba3.domanda: What is the characteristic of an absolute path?
9c7145142ba3.spiegazione: An absolute path starts from the root of the file system (with /) and works from any location; a relative path starts from the current directory.
risposte: Works only if the pwd command is executed first for verification
Always starts from the current location

68b8b6a8d99c.spiegazione: --amend replaces the last commit with a new one, which is useful for fixing a typo or adding a forgotten file without creating an extra commit.
risposte: To replace the current commit with a new one that includes staged changes and an updated message

9b334bb6838e.domanda: Where must the .gitignore file be located to be recognized by Git?
9b334bb6838e.spiegazione: The .gitignore file should be placed in the project root, in the same location as the .git directory, to be recognized.
risposte: In the project root directory, where .git is located
In the user's home directory of the operating system

578265a24421.domanda: When is it advisable to use squash & merge instead of a regular merge?
578265a24421.spiegazione: Squash & merge condenses the feature into a single commit: useful for a linear mainline history without noise, at the cost of losing atomic history.
risposte: When you want to condense the history of a feature into a single commit for a cleaner timeline

4435038943cf.domanda: In the most common workflow, how are rebase and merge combined?
4435038943cf.spiegazione: Common practice: use rebase to keep the feature branch up to date during development, then use merge --no-ff to record the integration point in main.
risposte: Use rebase to keep the branch up to date, then merge --no-ff to integrate it into main
Perform only a merge at the end of the day

cd2e1679522b.domanda: Inside .git, what does the refs/ subdirectory contain?
cd2e1679522b.spiegazione: refs/ stores branch and tag names as text files pointing to specific commits.
risposte: The user's personal settings for the code editor
All project file contents compressed in binary format
The complete history of commands typed in the shell

917361b94eb6.domanda: How do you write italic text in Markdown?
917361b94eb6.spiegazione: *text* produces italic; **text** produces bold, ~~text~~ produces strikethrough, and `text` produces inline code.

d91a3b6a28d0.domanda: What are badges used for in a README?
d91a3b6a28d0.spiegazione: Badges (usually from Shields.io) are small images at the top of the README that display information such as build status, license, or version.
risposte: They are mandatory, and without them GitHub does not display the README
They display information about the project
They are used solely to make the document more colorful and appealing

e61e32759684.domanda: Which command shows only the last 5 commits in a compact format?
e61e32759684.spiegazione: git log --oneline -5 displays each of the last 5 commits on a single line.

4c27b73a7931.domanda: What does the pipe operator | do between two commands?
4c27b73a7931.spiegazione: The pipe | sends the output of one command as the input to the next, allowing simple commands to be chained together (e.g., ls | wc -l).
risposte: Saves all the command's output into a text file
Sends the output of one command to the input of the next

20d6c8230994.domanda: Which command opens the full manual for a command?
20d6c8230994.spiegazione: man <command> opens the manual page (exit with q); alternatively, <command> --help displays a brief help message.

da0b57d825be.domanda: Which command prints the full path of the current working directory?
da0b57d825be.spiegazione: pwd (print working directory) prints the absolute path of the current directory.

2a2480910b21.domanda: What is the recommended length for a commit subject line?
2a2480910b21.spiegazione: The subject line should be kept to <= 50 characters (absolute maximum 72; beyond that, GitHub truncates with ellipsis).
risposte: It must be at least two hundred characters long
It is sufficient if it contains only a single letter of the alphabet
It must consist of exactly ten words, no more and no less

8c6172b1aa16.domanda: Why is a trailing space after a .gitignore rule a problem?
8c6172b1aa16.spiegazione: A trailing space silently breaks the rule: Git looks for a file whose name includes that space, and the rule never matches anything.
risposte: It silently breaks the rule: Git looks for a file name that includes that space and finds nothing

6f643c6e060b.domanda: What does the 'touch filename.txt' command do if the file does not exist?
6f643c6e060b.spiegazione: touch creates an empty file if it does not exist; if it already exists, it only updates the timestamp without changing its content.
risposte: Renames it by adding a progressive numeric suffix to the name
Deletes it immediately from disk without asking for any confirmation
Opens it immediately in the default text editor

80400d0ba239.domanda: What is the most important category of files to ignore?
80400d0ba239.spiegazione: The most important rule: always ignore secrets and credentials (.env, API keys, passwords, tokens).
risposte: Normal plain text files present in the project
Image files used within the project
Files written in the Markdown formatting language

5ad0b09e1736.domanda: Which commit type indicates a change only to the documentation?
5ad0b09e1736.spiegazione: docs indicates changes to documentation only; feat = feature, fix = bug fix, perf = performance.

47a29fe9230b.domanda: What does the Ctrl+R shortcut do in the terminal?
47a29fe9230b.spiegazione: Ctrl+R starts a reverse search through the command history; the Tab key is used for autocompletion.
risposte: Searches backward through the command history while typing

c65bf6e3a2d5.spiegazione: git add src/ stages all the files contained in the src directory.
risposte: Creates a new folder called src inside the project root
Moves the src folder into the remote repository
Deletes all files contained within the src folder

1baddb4678b9.domanda: In a merge commit, which parent does Git consider the 'official' path?
1baddb4678b9.spiegazione: Git treats the first parent as the official path (the branch you were on); the tilde (~) follows the first parent.
risposte: Neither, because a merge commit has no parents
The second parent, i.e., the branch that was merged into the current one
Both parents are treated equally by Git

32f4830f42b9.domanda: Which command helps find the commit that introduced a bug?
32f4830f42b9.spiegazione: git bisect allows you to walk backwards through commits to pinpoint exactly which one introduced a bug.

fb177d101fe8.spiegazione: origin is not a special keyword: it is simply the conventional alias for the remote URL, so you don't have to type it in full.
risposte: The conventional name always given to the main branch
A special reserved keyword internal to Git's operation
The very first commit created when a project starts

5a8e7499f24c.spiegazione: It shows the commits present on origin/main but not yet on the local main: useful as a safety check after a fetch.
risposte: Commits on origin/main that are not yet in the local repository
All commits in the entire project history starting from the first one
Only the commits you have created locally and not yet pushed

54a484be9f32.domanda: What does the tilde symbol mean in 'HEAD~2'?
54a484be9f32.spiegazione: HEAD~N means 'go back N commits from the current point'; HEAD~2 is two commits before HEAD.
risposte: Shows the two main branches of the repository simultaneously
Go back by 2 commits from the current point

e3bad2817cc4.domanda: How should the Cmder (Full version) file be handled after downloading?
e3bad2817cc4.spiegazione: Cmder (Full version) is used by extracting the zip into a folder; the handout recommends never opening .zip files directly.
risposte: It must be uploaded to GitHub before use
It must be opened directly from within the compressed zip file
It must be executed as an installer
It simply needs to be extracted (unzipped) into a new folder

c662d21d548d.domanda: What does it mean that 'review comments are on the code, not on the person'?
c662d21d548d.spiegazione: A review is a conversation: comments are about the code. They should not be taken personally, and the reviewer must explain what to change and why.
risposte: It means that being offensive during the review is allowed
It means that comments left by reviewers can be ignored
They should not be taken personally
It means that in practice, comments have no real value

22383950d968.domanda: What is the purpose of a release branch?
22383950d968.spiegazione: A release branch (e.g., release/v1.0) is a stable environment where only bug fixes are performed, while new feature development continues on main.
risposte: It is primarily used to contain and host documentation
To finalize a stable version where only bug fixes are allowed

cf4782e89a1b.domanda: Which filename is valid because Git recognizes it?
cf4782e89a1b.spiegazione: The name must be exactly .gitignore: .Gitignore or .gitignore.txt are not recognized (note the .txt added by some editors).

d613a1ad5ee3.domanda: Which command displays only the first 5 lines of a file?
d613a1ad5ee3.spiegazione: head -n 5 prints the first 5 lines; tail displays the last lines, less scrolls through long files (q to exit).

0dccc42c91ee.domanda: What is commit squashing before a merge?
0dccc42c91ee.spiegazione: Squash combines small/confused commits into a single clean one, usually with git rebase -i, changing 'pick' to 'squash'.
risposte: Combine multiple small or unclear commits into one
Duplicate all commits from the current branch onto another branch

6b52c70858ff.domanda: How does a VCS help prevent accidental overwrites?
6b52c70858ff.spiegazione: Without versioning, saving replaces what was there; a VCS makes every saved state recoverable, so no action is permanent.
risposte: Makes every saved state recoverable, so no single action is permanent

bc39fd342640.domanda: What do three dashes --- on a line by themselves create?
bc39fd342640.spiegazione: Three dashes --- on their own line create a horizontal rule.

1ae65a957080.spiegazione: git clone <url> <folder> downloads the repository into a folder with the specified name, instead of using the repository's default name.
risposte: Renames the remote repository to my-folder on the server
Clones the repository into a folder named my-folder instead of the default name

36a5c99059f5.domanda: In which three states does Git classify files in the working directory?
36a5c99059f5.spiegazione: Git classifies each file as untracked (never seen), modified (changed since the last commit), or staged (ready for commit).
risposte: Public to everyone, private to the author, and finally shared with the team
Open on disk, closed in the editor, and then permanently saved

64a94bad3048.domanda: In the 'simple team workflow', what is the rule regarding the main branch?
64a94bad3048.spiegazione: In the simple team workflow, main is long-lived, always contains working code, and you never commit directly to it: you work on feature branches via PRs.
risposte: The main branch should be deleted immediately after every version release
You commit directly to main multiple times a day during work
The main branch is considered a temporary and intermediate branch

adf0f41677b8.domanda: What is the purpose of a .gitignore file?
adf0f41677b8.spiegazione: .gitignore lists files/folders to ignore (e.g., node_modules/, .env, *.log): they are never staged or committed, even with git add .
risposte: To encrypt secret files containing project credentials
To automatically create new branches on every commit operation
To tell Git what to ignore
To list all authors who contributed to the project

4c5ff31b1428.domanda: What are the four GitHub tabs mentioned as the ones to know?
4c5ff31b1428.spiegazione: The tabs to know are Code (files and commits), Pull requests, Issues, and Settings (access, default branch, protections).
risposte: Only the two main tabs, i.e., the Code tab and the Settings tab of the project
The files tab, the automatic tests tab, the wiki tab, and the Actions tab
The tabs dedicated to profile, notifications, organizations, and personal settings

74755ffe58a0.domanda: Which command shows which .gitignore rule is ignoring a file?
74755ffe58a0.spiegazione: git check-ignore -v filename shows the path, line number, and exact rule that ignores the file; empty output = not ignored.

4ba68a5e7347.spiegazione: git add . stages all changes in the current directory and its subdirectories.

f9589319ba53.domanda: What is the version history of a document?
f9589319ba53.spiegazione: Version history automatically records every change, like a photo album of the document, allowing you to revert to previous states.
risposte: The concept that every change is automatically recorded, allowing you to revert to any previous state

5e66570f7866.domanda: In a repository with no commits yet, how do you unstage a file?
5e66570f7866.spiegazione: In a new repository without commits, 'git restore --staged' may fail: use git rm --cached, which works with or without commits.
risposte: With git rm --cached <file>, which works even without commits
By executing a forced push to the shared remote repository

8138ad694570.domanda: What does 'git config --global merge.tool vscode' do?
8138ad694570.spiegazione: That command sets VS Code as the merge tool; then 'git mergetool' opens the visual tool on conflicting files.
risposte: Sets VS Code as the default visual tool to resolve merge conflicts

66ff71bad0b0.spiegazione: --name-only lists only which files have changed in the commit (in this case, the one before HEAD), without showing the diff.
risposte: Only the names of changed files
The complete list of all branches and tags present in the local repository
All modified lines line by line in the previous commit with colors
The detailed message of every commit in the entire project history

d024a1b02ee0.spiegazione: If main has no new commits since the branch was created, the merge is fast-forward: the main pointer advances without creating a new commit.
risposte: A merge that deletes the branch
When main hasn't changed since the branch was created, Git moves the pointer forward without a new commit

2a8cea2a88e0.domanda: Which of these is a commit message to avoid because it is vague?
2a8cea2a88e0.spiegazione: Messages like 'fix stuff', 'updates', 'wip', or 'saved' are valid but useless as documentation: months later, no one understands their meaning.
risposte: Fixes the navigation bar alignment on mobile devices
Adds email field validation in the registration form
Fixes the crash that occurred when submitting an empty password

e4bc6c43234b.domanda: What are the three main benefits of atomic commits?
e4bc6c43234b.spiegazione: Advantages: safe rollbacks (targeted revert), faster debugging (small snapshots), and more readable reviews.
risposte: Less disk space, higher speed, and more branches
Automatic code compilation, testing, and continuous deployment

04981a596c2d.domanda: What three basic questions does a version control system answer?
04981a596c2d.spiegazione: A VCS records changes over time by answering: what changed, who changed it, and when.
risposte: How heavy the project is, where it is stored, and at what time it was opened
Whether the code compiles, whether it runs, and whether it passes all expected tests
Who pays for the work, who approves it, and who handles the release

b08a92281b0e.domanda: What is a repository in Git?
b08a92281b0e.spiegazione: The repository contains the project and its entire history: every file, every version, commit messages, branches, and tags.
risposte: The project container and its complete history: files, versions, messages, branches, and tags

639efa84f39b.domanda: Why run 'git pull origin main' before creating a new feature branch?
639efa84f39b.spiegazione: If the local main is outdated, the created branch lacks recent commits, which increases the likelihood of future conflicts. Always pull main first.
risposte: If main is outdated, the branch is created without recent commits
Because this operation significantly speeds up the subsequent push

f2e55fb5998b.domanda: Why are Conventional Commits designed to be machine-readable?
f2e55fb5998b.spiegazione: The structured format of Conventional Commits allows automated tools to generate release notes and determine whether a new version number is required.
risposte: To enable automated tools to generate release notes and decide the version number

07ec32aa2cc9.domanda: How do you remove an untracked file in Git?
07ec32aa2cc9.spiegazione: An untracked file is not known to Git: it is simply deleted from the file system; Git has nothing to revert.
risposte: It is removed from the index with git restore --staged <file>
It is deleted from the disk
The git revert command is used, specifying the name of the file to remove
A git reset --hard is executed to completely clean the state

4b9927853690.domanda: Which shortcut opens the Markdown preview in VS Code?
4b9927853690.spiegazione: In VS Code, when opening a .md file, Ctrl+Shift+V opens the live preview panel.

7f904b4cebb6.spiegazione: ls lists files and pipes them to wc -l, which counts lines: thus counting the files in the directory.

684fd0103740.domanda: Which keyword in a PR description closes issue #42 upon merge?
684fd0103740.spiegazione: Keywords such as Closes #42, Fixes #42, or Resolves #42 in the PR description close the issue upon merge.

008ae60a4c6e.domanda: In the output of a diff, what do lines starting with + indicate?
008ae60a4c6e.spiegazione: In a diff: '-' = removed lines, '+' = added lines, no prefix = unchanged lines.

33a42bdc13e9.domanda: What is the purpose of the # character in a .gitignore line?
33a42bdc13e9.spiegazione: Lines starting with # are comments and are ignored by Git.
risposte: Creates an exception to a previously written rule
Indicates a comment: the line is ignored by Git

c2f15023f61a.domanda: Why is it beneficial to name a version in Google Docs?
c2f15023f61a.spiegazione: Docs can merge older versions to save space; naming a version preserves it, because named versions are never merged.
risposte: Because named versions are never automatically merged, unlike older unnamed ones

f9f35a3663ca.domanda: What does 'git commit' without the -m flag allow you to do?
f9f35a3663ca.spiegazione: Without -m, git commit opens the default editor (Vim, Nano, or VS Code) to write a multi-paragraph message.
risposte: Opens the default text editor to conveniently write a multi-line message

e0b35dcb3779.domanda: How do you exit the 'less' command while scrolling through a file?
e0b35dcb3779.spiegazione: You exit less by pressing the q key (quit).
risposte: By completely closing the terminal window you are using
By pressing the Ctrl plus Alt plus Del key combination
By typing the word exit followed by pressing the Enter key

96e7ebc48b7f.domanda: What is the difference between git init and git clone?
96e7ebc48b7f.spiegazione: git init starts with an empty repository without history; git clone downloads an existing repository complete with history and configures the origin remote.
risposte: git init creates an empty repository without history, while git clone copies an existing repository with its entire history

20908c93f6ac.domanda: What does the command 'diff file1.txt file2.txt' do?
20908c93f6ac.spiegazione: diff compares two files and displays the differences between them.
risposte: Displays the differences between the two files
Copies file1 into file2, overwriting it
Deletes the second file specified in the command

a9fa7a25655d.domanda: What does an audit trail guarantee in a VCS?
a9fa7a25655d.spiegazione: In professional or regulated environments, it is necessary to know who changed what and why: the VCS creates a permanent and attributed record.
risposte: Compression of the history to occupy less disk space
Sending commits to a second remote backup server

5dc02f6912f9.domanda: Why should you not rebase a branch used by other people?
5dc02f6912f9.spiegazione: Rebase rewrites history: on a shared branch, it breaks others' copies. It should only be done on local, unpublished commits.
risposte: Because it is a much slower operation than a normal merge
Because it always requires repository administrator privileges
Because it physically deletes all files present in the branch

550ff89bc457.domanda: What does 'git diff' show without any additional arguments?
550ff89bc457.spiegazione: git diff compares the working directory with the staging area: it shows changes that are not yet staged.
risposte: Changes made but not yet staged, comparing the working directory and the staging area

39058371b44d.domanda: What is the alternative name for the staging area?
39058371b44d.spiegazione: The staging area is also called 'index': the two terms refer to the same concept.

1561f1c6d1b1.domanda: Why in many teams is it not the person who opens the PR who clicks 'Merge pull request'?
1561f1c6d1b1.spiegazione: In most teams, it is the reviewer or a senior member who performs the merge, after the PR has been approved and agreed upon.
risposte: Because performing the merge requires paying a GitHub subscription
Because the merge button is not visible to the request author

131571556134.domanda: Why is it better to use relative links instead of absolute URLs in the README?
131571556134.spiegazione: Relative links (e.g., ./docs/setup.md) remain valid after cloning the repo and do not break if branch names change.
risposte: Because they remain functional when the repository is cloned and do not break if branch names change

a83c00628fdd.domanda: In the commit subject line, what should you not do?
a83c00628fdd.spiegazione: The subject line is a title: it should not end with a period, and vague words like 'fix stuff' or 'wip' should be avoided.
risposte: Try to keep it as short and concise as possible
Write it using the imperative mood as if it were a command
Use a verb at the beginning to describe the action taken

e63fcb724ec4.domanda: What does the config file inside the .git folder contain?
e63fcb724ec4.spiegazione: The config file holds repository settings, such as the remote URL.
risposte: The complete list of all commits with author and date
The repository settings, such as the remote URL

b8d2c42bedfb.domanda: Which command aborts an ongoing merge, restoring the previous state?
b8d2c42bedfb.spiegazione: git merge --abort cancels the ongoing merge and restores the previous state.

5b24d03cf4b0.domanda: On GitHub, in which tab do you comment on PR changes line by line?
5b24d03cf4b0.spiegazione: In the 'Files changed' tab, green lines are additions and red lines are removals; hovering over the line number opens the box to comment.

0e002f92e6e9.domanda: How do you create a heading in Markdown?
0e002f92e6e9.spiegazione: Use # followed by a space; the number of # indicates the level. Use only one H1 per document and do not skip levels.
risposte: By prefixing the @ symbol to the line that serves as the document title
By placing three asterisks before and after the title text
By enclosing the title in a pair of square brackets

47d9d04ab6e5.domanda: Which symbol creates a blockquote in Markdown?
47d9d04ab6e5.spiegazione: The > symbol at the beginning of a line creates a blockquote, used for notes or important callouts.

62fb1095df35.domanda: What is a common mistake in code review described in the lecture notes?
62fb1095df35.spiegazione: Typical errors: reviewing too quickly and skipping lines, saying 'it's wrong' without explaining, approving code that hasn't been understood, and taking comments personally.
risposte: Always clearly explaining what should be changed and why
Carefully reading every single line of code that has been modified
Honestly admitting not having understood a certain part of the code

023439d87326.domanda: Why is Git valuable even for a solo developer?
023439d87326.spiegazione: Even when working alone: you can experiment without risks (every state is recoverable), you have a project journal, use git bisect for bugs, and have an offsite backup with push.
risposte: Allows safe experimentation, tracking history, finding bugs, and having a remote backup

166b6efe70f0.domanda: Why does the appendix suggest using 'git commit' without -m?
166b6efe70f0.spiegazione: Without -m, git commit opens the editor (e.g., VS Code): it is easy to write multi-line messages and see the character count.
risposte: Because it opens the default editor and allows writing multi-line messages while seeing the character count

5a7a5d5d015c.domanda: Which ls flag also shows hidden files (those starting with a dot)?
5a7a5d5d015c.spiegazione: ls -a lists all files, including hidden ones that start with a dot (e.g., .gitignore, .env).

964d619ee20c.domanda: What does the alias 'git config --global alias.lg ...' suggested by the guide allow you to do?
964d619ee20c.spiegazione: The lg alias is set to 'log --graph --oneline --decorate --all', so you only need to type git lg to view a tree log of the repository.
risposte: By typing 'git lg' you get a colored tree log of the repository

74be7e98cc14.domanda: In the .gitignore file, what does the pattern '*.log' do?
74be7e98cc14.spiegazione: The asterisk is a wildcard: *.log ignores every file that ends with .log.
risposte: Ignores a file that is named exactly log
Automatically creates a new log file inside the project
Ignores the entire folder named log

006e49b439ef.domanda: Which two commands is 'git pull' a shortcut for?
006e49b439ef.spiegazione: git pull = git fetch (downloads) + git merge (merges) of the remote branch into the current local branch.
risposte: The git clone command followed immediately by git init
First git add and then the git commit command
The git status command followed by the git log command

d833f8d362fc.domanda: Comparing where the history is stored, how are Google Docs and Git described?
d833f8d362fc.spiegazione: Google Docs is centralized on Google's servers; Git is distributed: everyone has the full history locally and can work offline.
risposte: In this comparison, Git is centralized
Both are centralized systems on the company's servers
Docs is centralized, Git is distributed

d6c86bf80b5a.spiegazione: A PR is a GitHub feature (not a Git command) used to request merging your branch into another, enabling comments and reviews.
risposte: A formal request, a GitHub feature, to merge your branch into another branch (usually main)

690cf234de12.domanda: Comparing Git and SVN, how are branches in Git?
690cf234de12.spiegazione: In Git, branches are lightweight pointers to commits: cheap and fast to create. In SVN, they are directory copies on the server, which are heavier.
risposte: Heavy directory copies that are created directly on the central server
Only available when there is an active connection to the server
Physically duplicated folders inside the project's working directory

f985ce0bb90c.domanda: When is the version history not accessible in Google Docs?
f985ce0bb90c.spiegazione: Version history is only available with edit permissions; it cannot be accessed with view-only or comment-only permissions.
risposte: Only during nighttime hours due to maintenance
When you have been offline for less than an hour
When the document is too long and contains many pages of text

c1788be185da.domanda: How many H1 headings should a Markdown document have?
c1788be185da.spiegazione: Only one H1 is used per document (it serves as the title); main sections use H2, without skipping levels (e.g., do not go from H2 to H4).
risposte: None, because H1 is not supported by most common parsers
At least three, one for each of the initial parts of the text
As many as there are main sections in the document

351d07202634.domanda: Which scope should be selected when creating a PAT for normal repository work?
351d07202634.spiegazione: For basic git work, the 'repo' scope should be selected; the lecture notes also suggest setting an expiration (e.g., 90 days) instead of 'No expiration'.
risposte: repo, which covers basic repository work

7ccb2e8b666d.domanda: What is the suggested commit message format in Git Fundamentals?
7ccb2e8b666d.spiegazione: The format is 'type(scope): short description', with type being feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, chore.
risposte: An initial hashtag followed by a brief textual description
A sequential number followed by a descriptive title of the commit
The date, then the time, and finally the name of the commit author

74924c9191d3.domanda: Which modern command creates a new branch and immediately switches to it?
74924c9191d3.spiegazione: git switch -c <branch> creates the branch and moves HEAD to it; 'git branch' only creates it without switching.

0daaec86b459.domanda: Which command sets 'main' as the default branch for new repositories?
0daaec86b459.spiegazione: git config --global init.defaultBranch main sets main as the global default for new repositories.
risposte: It is sufficient to run the command git init main
The command git branch is used, specifying the name main
It is set by the command git switch main alone

5272d12c534d.domanda: How do you remove a file from the staging area while keeping the changes?
5272d12c534d.spiegazione: git restore --staged <file> moves the file from the staging area back to the working directory without losing the changes.
risposte: git reset --hard delete the desired file from the folder

29436a1f2e3b.domanda: Which command searches for a text pattern within a file?
29436a1f2e3b.spiegazione: grep searches for a word or pattern inside a file; with -i it ignores case, and with -r it searches recursively.

2675815b72d9.domanda: In Google Docs, how do you find out who last modified a specific row?
2675815b72d9.spiegazione: Right-click on the word or row and select 'Show editors': it shows who last changed that content and when.
risposte: By exporting the document to PDF format and checking the metadata
By opening the side comment panel and searching through replies
By manually scrolling through the entire document version history

69a9aa67f2c8.domanda: What is used instead of a password when pushing via HTTPS to GitHub?
69a9aa67f2c8.spiegazione: GitHub no longer accepts plaintext passwords: via HTTPS, a Personal Access Token (PAT) is used instead of the password.
risposte: The same password used to access the email account
A key from the installed Windows operating system product
The phone number linked to the personal GitHub account

332db99a9c69.domanda: What should the body of a commit message explain?
332db99a9c69.spiegazione: The diff already shows the 'how'; the body should explain the 'why': the problem solved or the decision made.
risposte: The reason for the change (the problem solved, the intent), not the how, which the diff already shows

b6ec70af0099.spiegazione: mkdir -p creates the entire directory chain, including any missing parent directories, in a single command.
risposte: Creates the directory and all missing parent directories in one go
Lists the contents of the directories specified in the path

570994998897.domanda: Which command reverts a tracked file to its last committed state?
570994998897.spiegazione: git restore <file> discards changes in the working directory, restoring the file to its last committed state (permanent operation).

5aa74448d2a7.domanda: Which site automatically generates .gitignore rules based on OS, editor, and language?
5aa74448d2a7.spiegazione: gitignore.io (Toptal) generates .gitignore templates based on the operating system, IDE/editor, and programming languages used.

ee3c54e87fce.domanda: What does the 'feat' type indicate in a commit message?
ee3c54e87fce.spiegazione: feat = new feature; fix = bug fix; docs = documentation; style = formatting; refactor = refactoring; chore = maintenance.

03c55b38dd9a.domanda: Why is it advisable to create an empty repository on GitHub if you already have a local project?
03c55b38dd9a.spiegazione: By initializing the remote with files, its history differs from the local one, and the first push fails ('unrelated histories'): it is better to start empty.
risposte: Because the added files take up too much space on the remote server
Because GitHub would delete them anyway during the first push
Because otherwise creating the repository becomes much slower

b6884a9e64fc.domanda: What does a reviewer typically look for during a code review?
b6884a9e64fc.spiegazione: The reviewer checks that the code does what the PR claims, that it has no obvious bugs, that it is clear, and that it respects the team's naming and formatting conventions.
risposte: Whether the code does what the PR claims, if there are bugs, if it is clear, and if it follows the team's standards

a4046d1aed9f.domanda: What are the three main reasons to use a .gitignore?
a4046d1aed9f.spiegazione: A .gitignore keeps the repository clean (no temporary/build files), protects secrets (API keys, .env), and reduces conflicts on machine-specific files.
risposte: To make it easier to rename, move, and copy files
Speed up pushes, encrypt files, and automatically create new branches
To allow compiling code, running tests, and deploying

a1557a5888a9.domanda: What is the purpose of the --no-ff option in 'git merge --no-ff'?
a1557a5888a9.spiegazione: --no-ff forces the creation of a merge commit even when a fast-forward would be possible, to keep track of the branch's existence.
risposte: To always create a merge commit even when a fast-forward would be possible, to track the branch

6be89c41004a.domanda: How do you correctly NOT ignore a file inside a folder that is otherwise ignored?
6be89c41004a.spiegazione: If you ignore the entire folder (logs/), Git no longer looks inside, and negation does not work: you ignore the contents (logs/*) and then make the exception.
risposte: Ignoring the contents with logs/* and then adding the exception !logs/config.php
It is not possible in any way to make such an exception
Deleting the .gitignore file entirely from the project

548ef38ecef7.domanda: Which command checks the installed version of Git?
548ef38ecef7.spiegazione: git version prints the installed version of Git on the machine.

fc18213d8880.domanda: Which command lists remotes with their full URLs?
fc18213d8880.spiegazione: git remote -v (verbose) lists remotes with their full URLs.

f03b2cc06929.domanda: When does a merge conflict occur?
f03b2cc06929.spiegazione: A conflict arises when two branches modify the same lines of the same file: Git stops and asks the user to decide.
risposte: When two branches of the repository happen to have the exact same name
When the remote server is offline during the merge operation
When the commit completely lacks a descriptive message

ce353f7867cd.domanda: What is Git Bash, as mentioned among the tools?
ce353f7867cd.spiegazione: Git Bash is a terminal for Windows that includes Git and a Unix shell, with utilities not available in Command Prompt: the easiest way to use Git on Windows.
risposte: A Windows terminal that includes Git and a Unix shell with utilities not present in Command Prompt

c69a005e9755.domanda: What is the final step in the lifecycle of a pull request?
c69a005e9755.spiegazione: Lifecycle: branch push, PR opening, review, any modifications, approval, merge, and finally deletion of the feature branch.
risposte: The feature code is written with the first local commits
After approval and merge, the feature branch is deleted

7a58d9f36f4b.domanda: What is the daily workflow cycle with a remote?
7a58d9f36f4b.spiegazione: Each session: Pull (you download updates), Work (you modify and commit locally), Push (you send commits to the remote).
risposte: You clone, then init, and finally merge the project
First push, then pull, and finally delete the branch

c715c3790b6a.domanda: When is the blank line between the subject and body of a commit mandatory?
c715c3790b6a.spiegazione: If there is a body, the blank line between the subject and body is mandatory: without it, some tools treat everything as a single subject line.
risposte: Only when the commit modifies more than a single source file
Only if using the Conventional Commits style with a scope
Only when the commit message exceeds seventy-two characters

0ff50b8ba201.domanda: Comparing Google Docs and Git, how does snapshot saving work?
0ff50b8ba201.spiegazione: Google Docs takes automatic snapshots; Git requires a manual and deliberate commit with a message explaining the change.
risposte: In both cases, snapshots are saved automatically
Docs saves automatically, Git lets you choose when (commit)

6533644c18bd.domanda: How are commits made in a detached HEAD state recovered?
6533644c18bd.spiegazione: To preserve them, a branch is created at the current location: git switch -c my-recovery-branch.
risposte: By deleting the hidden .git folder and then running git init again
By downloading the entire project again with the git clone command
By executing a forced push to the remote with git push --force

0665862b024e.domanda: What is the purpose of the double dash -- in a command like 'git add -- -config.json'?
0665862b024e.spiegazione: The -- separates flags from filenames: it is used, for example, to add a file whose name starts with a dash.
risposte: To completely ignore the file specified immediately after the command
To separate options from filenames (protects names starting with -)

3917619412d9.domanda: What is the correct way to close multiple issues from a PR description?
3917619412d9.spiegazione: The keyword must be repeated for each issue: 'Closes #42, Closes #67'. The form 'Closes #42, #67' closes only issue #42.
risposte: It is not possible to close more than one
List only the issue numbers separated by a comma

b2e0cfe622c7.spiegazione: Each commit has a unique SHA hash (fingerprint), along with a timestamp, author, and message.
risposte: The IP address of the commit author's machine
The line number of the code that was changed
The name of the file that was last modified in the commit

dd1adca7f116.domanda: What happens to the version history when you restore a previous version in Google Docs?
dd1adca7f116.spiegazione: Restoring a version makes it the current one but does not delete the version history: all previous versions remain available, and you can undo the restoration by restoring a more recent version.
risposte: The restored version becomes the current one, but the version history is not deleted and everything remains available

61b1f1335c76.spiegazione: Markdown is a lightweight formatting language: it is written in plain text using keyboard symbols and rendered as a formatted page.
risposte: A lightweight formatting language that is written as plain text and becomes a formatted page

73c80b5e98c0.domanda: Which command is used only once to create a local repository from a remote one?
73c80b5e98c0.spiegazione: git clone is a one-time setup command that creates the local repository from a remote one: it is not part of the daily workflow.

a805ebce5fec.domanda: Which git log flag displays one line per commit with the short SHA and message?
a805ebce5fec.spiegazione: git log --oneline displays a compact line per commit with the abbreviated SHA and message.

dbf0f9a33691.domanda: Which command forces the addition of a file that would otherwise be ignored?
dbf0f9a33691.spiegazione: git add -f (force) adds a file even if it matches a rule in .gitignore.

aa43a06b4e9b.domanda: What is the purpose of the staging area?
aa43a06b4e9b.spiegazione: The staging area (or index) is the preparation zone: it allows you to selectively choose which changes are included in the next commit.
risposte: To select which changes to commit
To automatically send files to the shared remote server
To compress and reduce the size of the project history

ace45a45dc9b.domanda: Why does adding an already committed file to .gitignore have no effect?
ace45a45dc9b.spiegazione: .gitignore only ignores files that have never been tracked. For a file that is already committed, you must remove it from the index using git rm --cached (the file remains on disk).
risposte: Because Git needs to be restarted
Because .gitignore only affects files that have never been tracked: for a file already tracked, you first need to use git rm --cached

1d24de26aad7.domanda: What does the ! character do in a .gitignore rule?
1d24de26aad7.spiegazione: ! creates an exception: after '*.log', '!important.log' ensures that all logs are ignored except that one.
risposte: Creates an exception to a previous rule
Indicates that the rule should be applied recursively to every folder
Forces the file to be committed

a6cf6a19a22c.domanda: What should you do if you accidentally push commits to main in a shared repository?
a6cf6a19a22c.spiegazione: In a shared repository, reset --hard or push --force rewrite history and break other people's copies: in that case, contact the team lead immediately.
risposte: Do not use reset --hard or push --force because they rewrite history, but contact the team lead immediately

7e81b5375afc.domanda: What is the difference between a VCS and a simple backup?
7e81b5375afc.spiegazione: A backup saves copies at intervals; a VCS saves deliberate and described checkpoints (a fix, a feature), and the description is as important as the snapshot.
risposte: A VCS saves deliberate and described checkpoints that represent significant work, not just copies at intervals

14bb8585b4f1.domanda: What is the difference between git add "*.txt" and git add *.txt?
14bb8585b4f1.spiegazione: git add "*.txt" lets Git handle the pattern (safe and recursive); git add *.txt expands the pattern in the shell, which is less portable on Windows and not recursive.
risposte: With quotes, Git handles the pattern (recursive and cross-platform); without, the terminal expands it

7e7f45f1707b.domanda: Why does the lecture advise against running 'git add .' blindly?
7e7f45f1707b.spiegazione: You should run git status first, to know exactly which files will end up in staging.
risposte: Because that command is now deprecated in recent versions of Git
Because it deletes all modified files without asking for confirmation
Because it only works on Linux-based operating systems
Better to run git status first

b1e0a1626da9.domanda: What does the interactive 'git add -p' option do?
b1e0a1626da9.spiegazione: git add -p (patch) splits the changes of a file into hunks and asks for each one y (yes), n (no), or s (split), for cleaner commits.
risposte: Stages individual change hunks within a file, asking y/n/s for each

b1de8bcfe2f7.domanda: In the analogy, what does the 'published' main branch correspond to?
b1de8bcfe2f7.spiegazione: Main is like a published book; a branch is like a private draft: you publish (merge) only when the draft is ready.
risposte: A rough draft that is thrown away at the end of the work
A temporary folder created by the operating system for files
A private draft on which all modifications and experiments are made

bc31c5b3d44d.domanda: Which commands configure the name and email for Git globally?
bc31c5b3d44d.spiegazione: They are configured with `git config --global user.name "first name last name"` and `git config --global user.email "..."`.
risposte: git set name and git set email
git config --global user.name and git config --global user.email

83b13e9eda74.domanda: What is the 'Bracket Style' for commit messages?
83b13e9eda74.spiegazione: The bracket style places key information at the beginning: [area][type] imperative description, for quickly scanning the commit list.
risposte: A date inserted in square brackets at the start of the line
The author's name enclosed in parentheses at the start
An initial hashtag immediately followed by the linked issue number

66ecfac6d23b.domanda: What is the legacy syntax, still valid, for discarding changes to a file?
66ecfac6d23b.spiegazione: git checkout -- <file> is the legacy syntax for discarding changes; today git restore is preferred as it is clearer.
risposte: git checkout -- <file>, replaced today by the clearer git restore

02d2765a1a69.spiegazione: An atomic commit performs exactly one logical task: the concept of the atom as an indivisible unit applied to Git.
risposte: A commit that performs exactly one logical task and nothing else, indivisible like an atom

300bf169c1cb.domanda: In the four-zone analogy, what does placing items on the bed correspond to?
300bf169c1cb.spiegazione: The wardrobe represents the working directory, the items on the bed represent the staging area (selected but not yet 'packed'), and the closed suitcase represents the commit.
risposte: The staging area: you've chosen what to bring, but you haven't closed the suitcase yet

47fcdae40f90.domanda: What does 'git remote add origin <url>' do?
47fcdae40f90.spiegazione: git remote add origin <url> associates a new remote named origin with the local repository; remote remove deletes it, and set-url changes its URL.
risposte: Changes the URL of a remote that already existed
Adds a new remote named origin pointing to the specified URL

f08bfe6feec4.domanda: In the pantry analogy, why is centralized like a public library?
f08bfe6feec4.spiegazione: Centralized = one single library: if it burns down (server lost), the books disappear; if it's closed (server down), no one can work.
risposte: D there is only one building with all the books: if it burns down or is closed, no one can work

13ea6e2a2154.domanda: How do you create a code block with syntax highlighting?
13ea6e2a2154.spiegazione: Triple backticks are used on separate lines, with the language name written immediately after the opening backticks for syntax highlighting.
risposte: By enclosing the entire block within two pairs of square brackets
By prefixing the greater-than symbol at the beginning of each line of code
By placing three consecutive hyphens before and after the code
With three backticks and the language name
